scope: FMP-12a / fmp12a-rehearsal-receipt / candidate. Aggregates the 2/3/4-participant rehearsal requirement set across runner, metrics, session creator and fixtures, binds the F(n)/U(n) engine-metric and causal-corpus inputs consumed from #149 and #150, and records the honest non-run state and its blocking prerequisites. It does not assert CC00 acceptance, CC01-CC05 adoption, EMB00 adoption, issue 120 source-manifest acceptance, or any #141/#142 load result.

Fn.meaning: Pure CPU execution duration of TickServer() fixed simulation tick under population n

Un.meaning: Elapsed interval between successive engine Update() cycles under population n

dualHistogram.compatibility: Schema 1 envelope preserves TickCount and TickMilliseconds for legacy parsers while populating distinct SimulationTickMilliseconds and FrameMilliseconds histograms.
dualHistogram.bindingToPopulation: F(n) and U(n) are per-population records: the rehearsal populations 2/3/4 each require their own dual-histogram record, sampled under that population. No such per-population record exists because no rehearsal ran.

observedParserSupport.detail: Interval.parse reads SimulationTickCount/SimulationTickMilliseconds into simulation_tick_histogram and FrameCount/FrameMilliseconds into frame_histogram, alongside the legacy TickMilliseconds histogram at line 216.

guarantees: Frames with zero simulation ticks (accumulator < 0.05f) still invoke RecordFrameMetrics, preserving periodic 5-second interval metric flushes.
SimulationTickStart and SimulationTickEnd remain equal during 0-tick intervals without advancing tick counters.
Population counters (ConnectedClients, NpcCount, ActiveIncidents) hold prior values across 0-tick intervals without inventing zeroes.
Exact boundary carry guarantees SimulationTickEnd of interval k equals SimulationTickStart of interval k+1.
zeroTickFrameIntegrity.requiredFor: Every rehearsal population, because a 2~4-participant rehearsal is expected to contain 0-tick intervals and a whole-run frame metric must still flush across them.
